title: spec review: B2 v2: compact delta packets in planner_runs — decision_packet/grouped_packet delegate to planner_packet.build with changes since the previous decision, structured scout findings, memory titles; escalation packet on re-escalation; packet size into telemetry (P4, P10)
spec:
Why: planner_runs.decision_packet (planner_runs.py:43-107) and grouped_packet (1063-1090) rebuild a per-point packet with the full spawn packet inventory and 300-char scout summaries, no delta, no memory, no required-output section. planner_packet (merged) provides build(sections, *, goal, previous, changes, scout_findings, memory_hits, cap_chars) -> {text, chars, est_tokens, hash, sections, truncated, delta} and escalation_packet(...); B1 v3 (T-0741, merged) made run_group sections 4-tuples (point, ctx, route, classification) and records launch rows. Spec review of T-0743 folded in: the legacy DecisionPacket tests are rewritten, and the change scan reads the events table directly.
What (planner_runs.py; tests in tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py, tests/test_goals.py, tests/test_planner_runs.py):
- _packet_sections(sections) -> list of planner_packet section dicts: for each (point, ctx, route, classification): task = bus.get(point task id) for held points else None; reviews = [{path, line, issue} for every comment in failures.rejecting_reviews(task)] (max 10) when task; failures = the text of (task.resume_hint or task.result).failures when task; depends_on_statuses = [{id, status} for dep in task.depends_on via bus.get, KeyError -> status "missing"].
- _previous_launch(goal_id) -> the planner_runs record of this goal with the latest started_at that has a launch_id, or None.
- _changes_since(goal_id, cursor) -> list of {"task", "field", "from", "to", "ts"}: query the sqlite events table directly under bus.locked() — `select task_id, seq, ts, data from events where seq > ? and task_id in (<the goal id and its children ids>) order by seq` (parameterised, ids from bus.read() filtered by parent == goal_id) — never through bus.events and its global 200-row page; for each row's data dict, fields status, hold_reason, merged_into only; from = the previous value seen in the scan (or the value at cursor time when unknown -> None), to = new; keep the last 20 entries (newest last). cursor = previous["cursor_at_launch"].
- _scout_findings(goal_id) -> scout_evidence.normalize_findings(scout result) concatenated over the goal's done scout children (max 10, highest confidence first); _memory_hits(goal) -> up to 10 {title} from scout_evidence.memory_recall(goal title, root=STATE) guarded by try/except Exception -> [].
- grouped_packet(sections) -> planner_packet.build(_packet_sections(sections), goal=bus.get(goal_id), previous={"state_version": prev.get("state_version")} if prev else None, changes=_changes_since(goal_id, prev["cursor_at_launch"]) if prev else None, scout_findings=..., memory_hits=..., cap_chars=[planner].decision_packet_chars default 6000)["text"]; the full build result is kept on a module-level _LAST_PACKET_META so run_group stores packet_chars, packet_hash, packet_delta, packet_truncated on the records and passes packet_chars=build["chars"] to planner_telemetry.record_launch (replacing len(prompt)). decision_packet(goal_id, kind, payload, repo_path) (legacy single-point path) builds one section via build_ctx + planner_taxonomy.classify and returns build(...)["text"] (len <= cap); the legacy inventory, "Task title:"/"Scout summaries:"/"Spawn packet:" lines and 300-char summaries are removed. Rewrite tests/test_goals.py's DecisionPacket suite (lines ~616-707) to the new format: same scenarios, assertions on the planner_packet section headings (Decision, Goal, Relevant task state, Scout findings, Required output), the fenced untrusted text, and len(text) <= cap; keep the test method names.
- Escalation (P10): in run_group, when ctx.get("reescalation") is True and a planner_shadow row exists for this goal's previous launch (rows of runs/sched/planner_shadow.jsonl with goal_id, latest started_at), render the prompt from planner_packet.escalation_packet(goal=..., original_sections=..., opus_decision={proposed_action, summary, tasks_proposed, confidence, needs_fable, unresolved} from that row, unresolved=row unresolved, conflicting_evidence=None, scout_findings, memory_hits, reason=";".join(hard_reasons), cap_chars) instead of build; store packet_kind "escalation" vs "decision" on the planner_runs records (the launch row is unchanged).
- The rendered prompt still goes through spawn.render("planner-decision", packet=text).
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_first_decision_packet_has_sections_and_no_inventory — grouped_packet for a scouts_done goal with two done scouts and a patched memory_recall yields text containing 'first Planner decision for this goal', the Scout findings and Memory sections, no 'Spawn packet' section, and len(text) <= decision_packet_chars

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_delta_packet_reads_events_table_beyond_200_rows — after a first launch record with cursor_at_launch, 250 unrelated events on another goal followed by a child task changing status and hold_reason still produce a packet whose Changes section lists both fields with from/to and the previous state_version; the record stores packet_delta True and packet_chars equal to the build's chars, and the launch row's packet_chars matches

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_held_section_carries_failures_reviews_and_dependency_statuses — a held task with resume_hint failures, a rejecting review with two comments and one missing dependency renders failures (capped), the two comments as path:line issue, and 'missing' for the dependency

tests/test_planner_runs_packets.py::test_escalation_packet_used_on_reescalation — with ctx reescalation True and a prior planner_shadow row for the goal, the rendered prompt contains 'Escalation reason:' and 'Opus proposed decision', no 'Changes since previous decision' section, and the record has packet_kind escalation; without a shadow row the ordinary build is used

tests/test_goals.py::test_decision_packet_new_format — the rewritten DecisionPacket suite passes against planner_packet output (section headings present, untrusted hold_reason fenced, len(text) <= cap, no Spawn packet inventory) and the whole tests/test_goals.py module is green

risks.issue: _packet_sections is specced to get the held task via raw `bus.get(point task id)`, but the existing `_decision_task(goal_id, kind, payload_key)` helper (planner_runs.py:372) already does this exact id-parsing and explicitly catches KeyError -> None because a held task can be purged between hold and the next planner tick ('callers must treat that the same as Jev being unavailable, never raise'). If _packet_sections uses a raw bus.get instead of _decision_task, a purged held task raises KeyError and crashes packet building inside run_group's decision launch, a regression from the current decision_packet(), which already wraps this in try/except KeyError.

_memory_hits is specced as 'up to 10 {title} from scout_evidence.memory_recall(goal title, root=STATE)', but memory_recall() (a thin wrapper around the shared recall() skill) returns a dict {hits, layers_consulted, stopped_at, chars}, not a list of hit dicts -- every existing caller (spawn.py:262-263, spawn.py:523-524) does memory_recall(...)['hits'] before touching titles. If _memory_hits skips that ['hits'] extraction it will either crash or, since it's guarded by a bare try/except Exception -> [], silently return an empty Memory section in production. Because the acceptance test patches memory_recall directly, a mock shaped as a bare list would make the test pass while the real dict-shaped return breaks at runtime -- exactly the silent-fallback failure mode worth catching before implementation.

suggested_spec_changes: In the _packet_sections bullet, replace 'task = bus.get(point task id) for held points else None' with 'task = _decision_task(point["goal_id"], point["kind"], point["payload_key"])', reusing the existing helper so a purged held task degrades to task=None instead of raising.

In the _memory_hits bullet, spell out the extraction explicitly: '_memory_hits(goal) -> up to 10 {title} from scout_evidence.memory_recall(goal title, root=STATE)["hits"]', matching the ['hits'] pattern already used in spawn.py.

Note the module-level _LAST_PACKET_META hand-off from grouped_packet (text-only return, for backward-compatible tests) to run_group (which needs packet_chars/hash/delta/truncated) is global mutable state smuggled between two calls in the same function body; call out in the spec that grouped_packet and its meta read must stay strictly sequential/single-threaded within one run_group invocation, or better, have run_group call a private helper that returns (text, meta) directly and make the public grouped_packet(sections) a thin wrapper around it for the tests.
